entities.summary: Legal science or jurisprudence, also known as "legal studies," is the academic study of law, its forms, and its application. It is also the name of the academic discipline concerned with these matters. The discipline critically examines case law, legislative proposals, and their social impact, thereby making a fundamental contribution to the development of the legal system. Legal science should not be confused with legal practice: although legal practitioners work on the basis of legal scholarship, only a few of them contribute back to legal science itself, for example, as authors of legal journals or commentaries on legislation.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Legal science has shaped the development of modern legal systems and continues to influence contemporary debates on law and governance. Its critical examination of case law and legislative proposals has contributed significantly to the evolution of human rights and the rule of law.
